components.source_check: Opened pp. 1, 3-4: sigma-field as a (nonempty) collection closed under complements and countable unions, countable = finite or countably infinite, reason for omitting intersections, measurable-space gloss; sigma(A) on p. 3; algebra (or field) on p. 4 with closure under intersections derived.
components.gap: Preserve the source variants of the entry's two definitions. Durrett (sec. 1.1, p. 1) defines a sigma-field as a nonempty collection closed under complements and countable unions, gives his reason for leaving closure under countable intersections out of the definition (the shorter list is easier to check) and glosses a measurable space as a space on which a measure can be put; on p. 4 he defines an algebra, or field, by: A, B in the collection imply A^c and A union B in it, and derives closure under intersections from A cap B = (A^c cup B^c)^c. def:p15-sigma-algebra (handbook/parts/p15/measurable-probability.tex 25-47) states only forms that require Omega to belong to the collection; it never states their equivalence with the source's nonempty forms (nor that the empty collection meets the source's literal algebra conditions), the synonym field, the closure of an algebra under intersections, or the source's reason and gloss. Neither the route nor this packet's owned files supply them; they are drafted only in packet w02c-p15-014's unrouted file (handbook/parts/p15/limit-theorems-and-concentration-w02c-p15-014.tex 196-262, thm:p15-w02c-p15-014-sigma-field-variant).

blocker.ref: owned by w02c-p15-014: source forms of the sigma-field and field definitions, drafted in handbook/parts/p15/limit-theorems-and-concentration-w02c-p15-014.tex 196-262, not routed
